issues.description: The gloss defines the singular 'noodle', but the dialogue uses the natural plural 'noodles'. Learners may not connect the two forms without a hint.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a short note to the gloss, e.g.: '...you cook it in hot water. People usually say "noodles" (plural).'

issues.description: 'This night market has a lot of food' is grammatical and natural enough, but 'There is a lot of food at this night market' is the more idiomatic way to introduce a scene in English.
issues.suggested_fix: Optional: change to 'There is a lot of food at this night market.' Keep the current line if simplicity is preferred.

qa_report.summary: A clean A2 micro_dialogue. All three lines are grammatically correct and natural; the target word 'noodle(s)', the review words 'food' and 'eat', and the grammar point 'would like' for polite requests are all present and used correctly. The grammar note accurately states 'would like + noun / to + verb' and contrasts it with the less polite 'I want noodles'. Only two minor polish points: the gloss could flag the usual plural 'noodles', and line 1 could use the more idiomatic 'There is a lot of food...' pattern. No critical or major issues; approve.
